summary:
A2 is done in the worktree, nothing committed. The patch covering A1 + A2 is written and applies to HEAD. The hull part builds with build_hull_only (0.05 0.01 abs 40) as one hollowed, closed solid in 31-37 s; A1's build took 186 s.

**Sections.** section() is now ONE convex curve per station, using the corner-rounding superellipse from sections-6, from the keel or stem point to the deck edge. The φ/n/β tables are interpolated with a numpy PCHIP. The keel point, deck edge and strake height stay where they were. The waterline beam is now an output of the shape; WATERPLANE, WL_BEAM_FRACTION, SECTION_FULLNESS, fullness() and _table() are removed. wl_half_breadth() and displaced_volume_m3() now integrate the real section.
- The DWL crease is gone. On the STL hull sides (x 1500-6500, z ±300 mm), V9 has 1.35% of edges creased more than 5° and A2 has 0.00%. In V9, 44% of the creases over 2° sit at the DWL; in A2 it is 5%.
- Flare decreases upward: 26-37° at the waterline, 9-20° at the deck. The bilge radius is now 420-690 mm (it was 7-165 mm, right under the DWL).

**Deck edge.** A 25 mm radius is built into each station wire: side, round, deck, round, side, all joined tangentially. The OCC fillet that fails is not used. Circle fits on the STL give R = 25.0 mm at x=3200 and 24.9 mm at x=5000. The virtual corner is pushed out 4-11 mm so the round's plan silhouette lies on A1's deck line, which keeps the deck beam at 2680.0.

**Stem.** The V at the keel gets a small round foot, giving a stem radius of 18.8-23.6 mm in the STL waterlines (V9 measured 3.8-4.9 mm, i.e. a knife edge). The stem position is unchanged within 4 mm. A 15 mm round nose shrinks the bow cap from 174×9 to 123×6.4 mm.

**Loft.** Every station now uses the same arc-length parameters with explicitly scaled end tangents. The side faces have 28 u-knots instead of about 1010.

**OCC pitfall found and fixed.** Edge.makeSpline(tangents, scale=True) put a cusp into the starboard side spline at the bow. That alone produced 81k-100k non-manifold STL edges. With scale=False and tangents I scale myself, the final STL has 77 non-manifold edges (A1 103, V9 124).

**Main open issue.** On the convex sides, today's 55 mm-proud strake (package B) stands 14-29 mm outside the deck line, so the beam over the strake is 2725 mm. With B's planned 30-35 mm strake it sits -6 to +9 mm from the deck line.

This took about 2.5 h instead of 60 min, mostly diagnosing the mesher cusp.

changes.what: A2, on top of A1's splines. Replaced the two-piece section(): _pchip (numpy Fritsch-Carlson), _smin and _nose (bow outline rounded over BOW_NOSE_L) added. _section_geom(x), cached, builds the dense convex curve from the keel to the virtual deck corner. It contains: the corner-rounding superellipse; deadrise and flare limited by the chord angle at the tiny bow sections; the stem/keel foot round (STEM_R / profile slope, apex lowered so the curve passes exactly through bottom_z); the deck-edge round (R = DECK_EDGE_R, smoothly limited where the section is small) as a rational quadratic Bezier; and the virtual corner pushed out so the round's outermost point lies on deck_half_breadth. section(x, n) returns n points along arc length (denser at the keel) ending at the virtual corner, so section_inner/_side_frame/stand keep working. New section_parts(x) returns side/corner/deck point lists, fixed parameter lists and joint tangents for the loft. deck_arc spans the virtual corner. wl_half_breadth and displaced_volume_m3 now come from the section. Removed _natural_cubic/_table/fullness/_BW_MAX. section_inner unchanged, A1's last-crossing fix kept. CRLF and Norwegian comments without special letters kept.

_section_wire builds 5 edges per station: starboard side, deck-edge round, deck camber, port round, port side. Each is a spline with the same parameter list at all stations and explicitly scaled end tangents (scale=False), G1 at every joint. The comment documents the OCC scale=True cusp. hull_solid: BOW_STATIONS = (4, 8) added for the nose; stations from 10 mm, duplicate threshold 3 mm, n_pts default 28. transom_cutter, _strake_path, rubbing_strake untouched.

In the hull-section block, in place of SECTION_FULLNESS/WL_BEAM_FRACTION/WATERPLANE: SECTION_FLARE, SECTION_N, SECTION_DEADRISE (sections-6 values, PCHIP), DECK_EDGE_R = 25, STEM_R = 20, BOW_NOSE_L = 15, with comments citing the photos. A1's SHEER_SMOOTHING and CANOE_BOTTOM_HIDDEN are kept, as is everything else.

- Bilge minimum radius at x 2385-6360: 420-690 mm (A1: 7-165 mm).
- Flare at the waterline 26-37°, at the deck 9-20°.
- Curvature up the section: positive everywhere, no spike at the DWL (image 1).

BUILD (0.05 0.01 abs 40)
- One solid, hollowed. Build 31-37 s (A1 186 s). Plastic 231 cm3 (A1 230, V9 228).
- STL: 1,282,918 triangles, 64.1 MB (A1 855k / 42.8 MB).

WALLS AND STAND
- section_inner side wall 57 (45 + margin) at every station checked.
- In the STL, the void is ≥45 from the skin at the rounded deck edge (x 3200 and 5000).
- Stand cradles: valid single solids (36.3 / 38.2 / 56.9 cm3).

STRAKE (package B's part)
- Strake face minus deck line with STRAKE_PROUD 55: +14..+29 (≤ +16 amidships). Beam over the strake 2725 in the STL, 2711 analytic.
- With proud 35: -6..+9.
open_issues: Beam over the rubbing strake (package B's part): the convex sides carry today's 55 mm-proud strake 14-29 mm outside the deck line, so the STL beam is 2725 mm (+1.7%); the deck alone is 2680.0. With B's planned 30-35 mm strake it is -6..+9 mm. If B keeps 55 mm, raise SECTION_FLARE amidships: 10.5° gives about 2698 mm over the strake (analytic), 11.5° about 2689 mm. The cost is a waterline beam of 2104/2071 mm and a canoe body of 3.57/3.49 m3.

STL size and export settings (package D): a 25 mm (0.83 mm model) radius needs about 0.04 mm triangles at 0.05 rad. The fine STL is 1.28M triangles / 64 MB, against 855k / 43 MB for A1. A bare-loft test starting at x=50 gave the two deck-edge bands 449k/286k triangles at 0.05 rad and 64k/55k at 0.12 rad. An angular tolerance of about 0.1 for the hull would cut the size a lot.

OCC pitfall for anyone building splines: Edge.makeSpline(..., tangents=[t0, t1], parameters=..., scale=True) mis-scaled the starboard end tangent and put a cusp in the curve (speed ratio 0.0005). The result was 81k-100k non-manifold STL edges. hull.py now scales the tangents itself (scale=False). shell._inner_wire and stand still use makeSpline without tangents, which is unaffected.

Bow tip: the nose rounds only the first 15 mm. That is limited by the trace tolerance and by keeping the stem head at x=0 and LOA 7950; the drawn nose reaches about 22 mm ahead of x=0. A small flat cap of 123x6.4 mm (4.1x0.2 mm model) remains at x=4. A station at x=2 pinched the deck-edge round to 0.5 mm and added 196 non-manifold edges, so the loft starts at x=4. 10 non-manifold edges remain at the tip.

Transom top corner: the transom cut crosses the rounded deck-edge band and leaves two 127 mm2 islands of side face at x≈7866-7873, z≈925. The solid is valid and the islands are harmless, but package B's transom-edge work will meet this band.

Between stations the loft deviates from the analytic section by up to a few mm (3-6 mm at points on the topsides at x=3200/5000). V9 had about ±5 mm. The PCHIP tables are C1, so section curvature steps slightly at the table points every 0.10-0.15 LOA. Neither is visible in the renders.
README.md lines 59 and 118 still describe SECTION_FULLNESS and WATERPLANE. README is outside hr26/data/tools, so it is not in the patch and needs updating at merge.

The bow and stern close-up renders did not finish because other packages' jobs were using the CPU. The rounds are verified by circle fits on the STL instead: deck edge R 25.0/24.9 mm, stem R 18.8-23.6 mm. The 3/4 flat and smooth renders and the body plan are delivered.
This took about 2.5 h against the 60 min target, mostly finding the makeSpline cusp behind the 100k non-manifold edges.
